About the portal

The Sleep Disorder Knowledge Portal enables browsing, searching, and analysis of human genetic information linked to sleep disorders and related traits, while protecting the integrity and confidentiality of the underlying data.

Using the portal

  • Are you interested in looking up a specific gene in our GWAS results? You can enter a gene name in the search bar above to see genetic associations and epigenomic annotations for the region including the coding sequence and 50 kb of upstream and downstream flanking sequences.
  • Would you like to download summary statistics for recently published GWAS relevant to sleep and circadian traits? These are available on the Downloads page.
  • Would you like to learn more about how genetic association studies are conducted? See our Introduction to Genetic Association Analysis.

About the project

The Sleep Disorder Knowledge Portal is being developed by a team of scientists and software engineers at the Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard in collaboration with a team at Massachusetts General Hospital, and many collaborators from across the globe, with funding from the NIH National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI) and The National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases. The platform seeks to provide comprehensive quality-assured summary genome-wide association results and the statistical and visualization tools to enable testing of the most compelling hypotheses as rapidly as possible, translating genomic data into biological and therapeutic insights. The RRID of the SDKP is SCR_016611.

Getting started

Are you interested in what human genetics can tell you about your favorite gene, but not sure where to start in the SDKP? We've outlined a workflow that can help you assess the weight of genetic evidence for involvement of a gene in a biological process. See the workflow in a step-by-step guide or in this brief video.
